name: DC Half Marathon
typicalWeather: Five-year average of about 17 °C at the start and 26 °C in the afternoon (62 °F and 78 °F), per HalfRuns
summary: The DC Half is organised by Pacers Running and starts in West Potomac Park. The race site says runners pass the monuments in the first mile. HalfRuns describes the course as an ultra-flat, USATF-certified out-and-back along the Potomac River, with sections beside Rock Creek Parkway.
courseHighlights: Lincoln Memorial and Washington Monument views

paceStrategy.summary: The course is described as ultra-flat, so an even pace is the best plan. Warm September air is the main challenge, so start a little conservatively and drink early.

segments.advice: Start at goal pace or slightly slower in the crowd.

segments.terrain: Flat, along the river and parkway
segments.advice: Hold an even pace and take fuel and fluid on schedule.

segments.terrain: Flat return to West Potomac Park
segments.advice: Keep steady, and push only in the final mile if you feel good.

fuelingNotes: No aid-station positions were found on the pages we checked. HalfRuns warns that the weather is warm, so plan to drink at every stop.
tips: Dress for a cool start and a warm finish; HalfRuns shows about 17 °C at the start and 26 °C in the afternoon
Start conservatively in the warm air
Plan your walk or ride to West Potomac Park, because HalfRuns notes it can be a walk from public transport
Do not confuse this race with the Rock 'n' Roll DC Half in March; they are separate events

faq.question: Is the DC Half course flat?
faq.answer: Yes. HalfRuns rates it ultra-flat and USATF-certified. We found no official elevation figures.

faq.question: Where does the DC Half start?
faq.answer: The race site lists West Potomac Park as the start location.

faq.question: When is the DC Half held?
faq.answer: It is held in September, with a 7 a.m. half marathon start.
